en: Among them, R0.69P–R0.71P reaches the positive-entry temporal-packing boundary, while R0.71Q–U gives the boundaries for conditional incidence, genuine internal-entry, second-time-jet, and finite recurrence. R0.71V–W separates the fixed zero-level trace and rules out a data-uniform complete first-row ledger. R0.71X, within a fixed-dimensional small-coupling family, reaches the one-third endpoint; R0.71Y treats selected roots; R0.71Z gives the all-root slope-mass bound and launch-inclusive floor cancellation. R0.72A localizes the strong-coupling loss to the actual observation layer, R0.72B retains exact target-row participation, and R0.72C obtains phase-uniform exact-launch \(M^{-8/3}\) and fixed-positive tail \(M^{-3}\) as the sharp algebraic scales. R0.72D, on a shifted Rudin–Shapiro family, constructs a positive-time exact root, retains the full rotational charge, and obtains a normalized complete-root ledger that does not vanish but does not diverge. R0.72E returns to a fixed-carrier Bessel family and uses quantitative negative-Sobolev action to prove that the complete-root ledger, relative to the candidate \(D^{1/3}\Lambda_1\) payment, diverges like \(R^{4/3}\). R0.72F then uses regularly varying initial-layer weights to separate the selected-root \(1/3\) threshold from the Leray payment \(1/2\) threshold and identifies the minimal critical-log boundary. R0.72G, on an exact real one-carrier lattice, uses a phase gauge, the target-row identity, and Rolle–BV reduction to prove that the complete root mass is exactly of logarithmic order, yielding critical-log complete-root sharp saturation. R0.72H proves for the mixed row a carrier-count-independent moment-resolved payment; the all-odd Rudin–Shapiro family rules out the action-only version and makes the carrier power encoded by that moment attain the same order. R0.72I proves that the separated positive \(B_AQ_*\) term cannot be absorbed physically term by term, while joint exposure and odd-carrier parity prove uniform decay of the genuine complete ledger. R0.72J completes the bipartite classification of the gcd-reduced Cayley graph, distinguishes an odd cycle from a triangle return, and proves that a common-band coherent mixed-parity cubic still decays after physical normalization. R0.72K, through a root-by-root gap norming direction, closes the complete complex-target ledger and proves that its common-band physical normalization ratio still decays uniformly. R0.72L retains the actual enstrophy contrast and critical-log action and closes, as \(R\) grows, a moderate strong-coupling window; the upper edge of the window gives only \(O(1)\), while only the little-o subwindow decays. R0.72M determines the scalar action danger window exactly and, on the complete one-carrier zero-diffusion chain, proves the Bessel action-poor benchmark and sharp logarithmic cubic law. R0.72N rules out the declared launch action-poor route on the complete dissipative chain and, from Coble–He time-dependent shear decay, derives the site's corollary \(\mathcal C_{\rm diss}\lesssim a^2\sqrt\sigma\). R0.72O reinserts this cubic into the physical ledger, obtaining an \(\varepsilon^{11/6}\) numerator and an \(R^{4/3}L_{R,\varepsilon}^2\) window; the multicarrier statement is conditional on a full-superposition ED hypothesis with a uniform constant. R0.72P closes the complete propagation gate on the fixed real-collinear static-phase 1:2 positive class, and R0.72Q then, for fixed-\(M\), arbitrary-static-phase, and \(Q_2\le1/2\), proves the two-critical-point shape gate together with an exact 1:2 caustic. R0.72R constructs a four-real-dimensional rational polydisc lying entirely outside the old weighted cone, for every \(y\ge0\) closes full-heat-path root localization, and, for \(0\le y\le1\), closes the physical \((\pi/48,144,240)\) shape contract and coefficient-uniform fixed-pattern commensurate 1:2:3 triangular affine-row enhanced dissipation; the complete four-dimensional caustic stratification is unfinished. R0.72S further takes the fixed-first-harmonic \(1{:}2{:}3\) marked incidence preimages and classifies them exactly as \(A_2,A_3,A_4,A_5\), uses determinant \(5400\) to prove, modulo constants, the restricted miniversal property, and, for the pure-second \(A_2\) and real-even \(A_3\) heat paths, gives \(4/3/2\) and \(4/2/2\) as the distinct count; the latter is transverse only within the real-even slice. This does not complete the global caustic image or prove general three-dimensional Navier--Stokes regularity. R0.72T--W fixes and closes the exact scalar A2 collision block, and R0.72X then, on a fixed physical compact set, obtains the all-start A2 path; Bloch-uniformity still belongs only to that scalar path. R0.72Y starts from Navier--Stokes and rederives the complete Fourier--Leray row, pressure factor two, Orr--Sommerfeld--Squire triangularization, and velocity recovery, then separates, by spatial norm, the scalar invariant row's forcing conclusion: standard H^-1 spacetime transfer is alpha, semiclassical H^-1 spacetime transfer is alpha^2, and the standard endpoint has no vanishing alpha gain. The exact zero-coupling lift-up shows that epsilon-only full-row closure and every-row strict contraction are FALSE. R0.72Z, on the high-gap \(q\)-graph, closes signed OS pressure and orientation-paid Squire history; R0.73A uses the hidden physical mean to close a low-gap \(X_\mu\) finite transient; R0.73B then uses exact Bloch carrier cancellation to close the complete linear velocity/Squire rows' viscous-rate physical-kinetic direct sum. Thus the low-gap vector direct sum at viscous rates is CLOSED; the complete OS--Squire A2 direct sum, sharp \(|\Lambda|\) law, nonlinear Navier--Stokes, and Clay remain OPEN. R0.73C then uses the exact cubic neutral spectrum and a validated periodic-ODE monodromy sign certificate to prove an infinite-dimensional frozen Rayleigh instability; viscous fast-time transfer remains OPEN, and super-polynomial complete-row no-go is only CONDITIONAL. R0.73D then, in the exact kinetic space, proves static vanishing-viscosity persistence of the certified inviscid spectral cluster, operator-norm convergence of the Riesz projections, and preservation of algebraic multiplicity; the general precedent belongs to Shvydkoy--Friedlander, while the complement and fast-time transfer remain OPEN. R0.73E uses fixed-positive-half-plane completeness, a relative dichotomy for the complete top cluster, and a fixed-generator Volterra argument to close logarithmic fast-time transfer; the moving-profile fixed-window problem, complete OS--Squire, nonlinearity, and Clay remain OPEN. R0.73F then uses bounded-perturbation roughness, the exact clamped profile, and a moving unstable bundle to close a fixed-window exponential lower law for one exact linear row; the finite diagnostic, complete all-row problem, nonlinearity, and Clay remain separate. R0.73G then uses an explicit strong-norm bootstrap and an all-mode remainder energy estimate to upgrade this one-row lower bound to nonlinear relative amplification for an over-small seed; the selected real orbit remains strictly within a globally smooth two-dimensional subspace. The natural seed, order-one departure, transverse three-dimensional problem, and Clay remain OPEN.
